Printed once, only when nats-server is not on PATH and a root-owned, not group- or other-writable one (not a symbolic link, in a folder whose every ancestor is the same) is in /usr/sbin, /usr/local/sbin or /sbin (in that order); the folder in the line is the one found. No "nats-server:" prefix: only "error:" and "warning:" are prefixes.

items.case: signing.nk and signing.pub are both missing
items.text:
error: signing.nk and signing.pub are missing from <dir>
hint: mashctl init --config <file>
items.note: From ctl #1390. The signing refusals print in the specification's error rule: `error: <what>` then `hint: <command>`, on stderr, exit 1. <dir> is the key folder as the error carries it (the plain path). The public keys the earlier text printed are not in default output. They are left out of --json too: the error object has only `error` and `hint`, and cliframe has no detail slot for errors. Printed by every mashctl command that signs (endpoint create, reissue, delete) and by init for the first two cases.

items.case: The join file's user JWT is named for another address
items.text:
error: bob.join names acme.demo.bob but is for acme.demo.carol
hint: mashctl endpoint reissue acme.demo.bob --out acme.demo.bob.new.join
items.note: From ctl (final text, head f1c8b74; replaces ctl's earlier #1303 text). "names" is the address in the file; "is for" is the address its credentials were made for. When the credentials carry no name: `error: bob.join has no name but names acme.demo.bob`, same hint. The old line `error: mix.join is not a join file this mash can read` stays for every other join-file problem. The hint is run by whoever made the file.
items.replaces: error: mix.join is not a join file this mash can read

items.text:
error: port 4222 is in use (pid 12); nothing was removed
hint: mash-local-nats-setup.sh --remove
items.note: From mash-sdk (lead #833). One wording for one situation. --remove still refuses whenever the port is held, and the error names the holder by pid: "(pid 12)" for one, "(pids 12, 34)" for several, listed once each and nothing else printed about them; the pid and the port vary. No paths. The hint is the retry: the script has already run --stop before it checks the port, so what holds it is something else (for example a wrapper that runs nats-server); once that is stopped, --remove finishes. With a folder other than the default (~/mash-nats), the hint adds --dir <folder>. v0.5.8 printed a sentence for the hint. The "removing anyway" line is dropped: there is no remove-anyway path. The case where no pid is visible is not changed here.
items.replaces: error: something still listens on 127.0.0.1:PORT; nothing was removed

items.case: A shell reports what serve delivered
items.text:
(what serve refused is invisible at a shell; what serve delivered is
shown there with its label)
items.replaces: A refused message is invisible at a shell too
items.note: The text is policy's proposed text (spec/next.json at a827f3d2), in round brackets. REQ-013. A description, not output: the whole text is in round brackets, which the rules reserve for a description, so the conformance test skips it. A message serve recorded as refused stays refused at a shell, whatever the shell's accept-unverified setting. A message serve delivered under --accept-unverified shows at a shell with its trust label, whatever the shell's setting. A message no serve has judged yet is judged by the shell's own setting, as today. The existing "A message that was refused" case and the inbox listing are unchanged.
